news.headline: Nasdaq 100 Rallies as Oil Slides, Yields Retreat: Stock Market Today
news.summary: Wall Street snapped a two-day losing streak Thursday as oil retreated from its geopolitical spike and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped back below 5%. Chipmakers led the rebound, with Intel, AMD and Micron all posting outsized gains, while gold climbed 2.5% to $4,369 an ounce. The bounce came one day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first interest rate hike since 2023 and signaled at least one more this year.
news.content_text: U.S. stocks rebounded sharply Thursday, erasing two sessions of losses as crude oil retreated from its geopolitical spike and Treasury yields eased back below 5%, one day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first interest rate hike since 2023. The S&P 500 rose 1.1% to 7,635.21, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lagged with a 0.7% advance, up 365 points to 51,827.04.  The Nasdaq 100 outperformed, jumping 1.8% to 29,450.56. West Texas Intermediate fell 1.6% to $100.81 a barrel Brent dropped 2.5% to $103.23, a one-week low Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and a unanimous FOMC lifted the fed funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday and projected at least one further increase this year, citing inflation that remains too high at 3.4% and a labor market at effectively full employment. Treasury Yields Retreat, Volatility Cools The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.95%, down 8 basis points and back under the 5.04% level hit earlier this week, which had marked a 19-year high. The policy-sensitive 2-year yield slipped 6 basis points to 4.69%, while the 30-year eased 7 basis points to 5.30%. The CBOE Volatility Index slid 11.4% to 15.69, unwinding the fear premium built up around the Fed decision and the Middle East supply scare. Gold was the standout in commodities, jumping 2.5% to $4,368.71 an ounce as real yields retreated, with silver surging 4.1% to $65.86.  On the macro front, initial jobless claims fell 10,000 to 196,000, well below the 206,500 consensus and close to July’s 60-year low, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index slowed to 37.8 from 47.4 but comfortably beat the 32.1 estimate. news.headline: Bloom Energy Stock Climbs on Falling Oil and Bond Yields
news.summary: Bloom Energy shares are trading higher Thursday as lower oil prices and bond yields boosted data center infrastructure stocks.
news.content_text: Bloom Energy Corp . (NYSE: BE ) shares are trading higher Thursday along with other data center infrastructure companies as falling oil prices and bond yields help risk assets rebound. Here’s what you need to know . Bloom Energy shares are advancing steadily. Why is BE stock advancing? Stocks Rebound as Oil and Yields Retreat Wall Street clawed back sharply Thursday after two rough sessions in a row, helped along by crude prices backing off their recent geopolitical-driven spike and bond yields dropping under the 5% mark, all coming just a day after the Federal Reserve pushed through its first rate increase in roughly three years. WTI crude slipped 1.6% down to $100.81 per barrel, while Brent fell even further, dropping 2.5% to settle at $103.23, its lowest mark in a week. Wednesday’s decision saw Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and every voting member of the FOMC agree to bump the federal funds rate a quarter point higher, landing in a fresh 3.75%-4% range. Retreating crude prices matter for Bloom Energy less because of direct energy costs and more because they ease inflation worries, reducing pressure on the Fed and encouraging investors back into riskier growth names. Falling Treasury yields have a more direct effect: since Bloom remains a capital-intensive, still-scaling business, its valuation leans heavily on future profits, and lower yields make those future earnings worth more in today’s dollars. Lower yields also reduce the cost of financing Bloom’s ongoing expansion, whether through debt or equity, making today’s macro backdrop a tailwind. Generac Deal With Amazon Lifts Data Center Power Stocks Helping fuel enthusiasm in the sector specifically, Generac Holdings Inc . (NYSE: GNRC ) unveiled a fresh arrangement connected to Amazon’s data center expansion, granting Amazon’s investment arm the right to buy up to roughly 1.7 million shares priced just above $200 each, an option that could translate into an $8 billion stake if fully exercised. Vicor Corp . (NASDAQ: VICR ) gave the sector another reason to rally Thursday, revealing a non-exclusive licensing arrangement with an unnamed manufacturer covering its Vertical Power Delivery technology, hardware designed to efficiently route power into demanding AI and networking chips. Neither deal involves Bloom Energy directly, but both serve as read-throughs for the broader data center power market Bloom competes in. Generac’s multibillion-dollar backup power agreement with Amazon and Vicor’s AI chip power licensing deal both point to surging hyperscaler demand for on-site power infrastructure, trend investors likely see as validating for fuel cell providers like Bloom as well. BE Shares Are Rising BE Price Action: Bloom Energy shares were up 3.69% at $279.99 at the time of publication on Thursday, according to Benzinga Pro . news.headline: QUICK SPARK: Generac Soars Nearly 20% on $8 Billion Amazon Data Center Deal
news.summary: Generac opened 27.8% higher on a long-term generator supply agreement with Amazon, then eased to 19%. Initial deliveries total $2.4 billion.
news.content_text: Generac Holdings Inc. (NYSE: GNRC ) jumped 19.1% to $208.48 by late Thursday morning, pulling back modestly from an opening spike of 27.8% that had the stock poised for its best session ever. The catalyst for the move is a long-term supply agreement to provide industrial backup generators for Amazon.com Inc.’s (NASDAQ: AMZN ) global data center infrastructure. Initial deliveries total $2.4 billion across 2027 and 2028, with purchases potentially reaching $8 billion over the life of the deal. The agreement reprices Generac from a hurricane-season consumer name into AI infrastructure. Backup power has become a binding constraint on data center buildouts, and Amazon just locked up years of capacity with one supplier. The stock entered Thursday already up 41% over 30 days. QUICK CONTEXT: Generac Lands Amazon Data-Center Power Deal Generac disclosed on Sept. 16 that it entered a long-term supply arrangement tied to Amazon data centers, marking a major expansion of its role in backup power for large computing facilities. Under the filing, Generac issued Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings, an Amazon subsidiary, a warrant to buy up to 1.69 million Generac shares at $200.9266 each. About 307,954 shares vested immediately, while the rest vest as Amazon-related payments for data-center backup generators rise, up to $8 billion. The first deliveries under the arrangement are expected to total $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028. Generac said the warrant can be exercised through Sept. 16, 2033, and is subject to standard adjustment provisions. Generac is a Wisconsin-based energy technology company founded in 1959. Its products include power generation equipment, energy storage systems, energy management devices and other power products for residential, commercial, data center, telecom, rental and industrial markets. The deal matters because Generac has traditionally been associated with home and business backup generators, but data centers are becoming a larger power-reliability market as cloud and AI workloads increase the need for resilient electricity infrastructure. news.content_text: Illumina (NASDAQ: ILMN ) has outperformed the market over the past 20 years by 4.87% on an annualized basis producing an average annual return of 13.99%. Currently, Illumina has a market capitalization of $34.28 billion. Buying $1000 In ILMN: If an investor had bought $1000 of ILMN stock 20 years ago, it would be worth $13,791.05 today based on a price of $224.19 for ILMN at the time of writing. news.headline: Beyond Hype: Twist Bioscience Secures Data Pipeline Role In Eli Lilly TuneLab Ecosystem
news.summary: Twist Bioscience joins Eli Lilly's TuneLab platform, supplying high-throughput antibody data to train advanced AI drug prediction models.
news.content_text: Twist Bioscience Corporation (NASDAQ: TWST ) on Wednesday announced an agreement with Lilly TuneLab, a collaborative AI/ML drug discovery platform created by Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE: LLY ) . Twist is a provider of antibody characterization data services for TuneLab, including for AbLab, an antibody developability prediction model. Read Also: Twist Bioscience Stock Resilient Despite Scorpion Capital Short Report Integrating High-Quality Wet Lab Data With AI Drug Discovery TuneLab was created to accelerate biotech innovation by enabling participating companies to access AI/ML drug discovery models trained on decades of Lilly’s proprietary research data. Participating companies may use the TuneLab prediction models to more rapidly down-select candidate molecules. Through this agreement, users will be able to order antibody services from Twist using TuneLab preferred Twist protocols to generate high-quality wet lab data. Leadership Commentary On AI Data Scaling And Federated Training “Twist has the scale and high-throughput capabilities to generate consistent and reliable antibody characterization data these models need to be trained on. Lilly’s leadership in empowering AI-enabled drug discovery and its impressive network of partnerships create a powerful ecosystem that brings together advanced models and high-quality data,” said Emily Leproust , CEO and co-founder of Twist Bioscience. In August, Anthropic selected Twist Bioscience as an independent evaluator for a protein design campaign using its Claude Opus 4.8 and Mythos Preview artificial intelligence models . Anthropic disclosed the results in an Aug. 18 blog post. Twist Bioscience subsequently reported the development in a regulatory filing. TWST Price Action: Twist Bioscience shares were up 5.79% at $146.09 at the time of publication on Wednesday. The stock is approaching its 52-week high of $155.44, according to Benzinga Pro data . news.headline: Elon Musk's Starlink Not a Threat to Wireless Carriers, Says T-Mobile CFO: ‘You Can Have a Million Satellites…’
news.summary: T-Mobile CFO Pete Osvaldik says Starlink can't replace wireless networks due to signal limits, though it may aid rural broadband.
news.content_text: T-Mobile US Inc. ‘s (NASDAQ: TMUS ) Chief Financial Officer Pete Osvaldik says that Space Exploration Technologies Corp. ‘s (NASDAQ: SPCX ) Starlink is not a threat to traditional telecom operators. The Fundamental Laws of Physics Osvaldik, speaking at Citigroup Inc. ‘s (NYSE: C ) 2026 Global TMT Conference on Wednesday, pushed back on the idea that satellite-to-phone service can replace traditional wireless networks. The company argued that distance-related signal limits make the technology unsuitable as a full alternative, especially indoors. Read Also: Bernie Sanders Sounds Alarm on 'Threat of Uncontrolled AI' as Geoffrey Hinton Puts 10% Odds on AI Killing Humanity: 'We’ve Got to Stop Right Now' “By the time the signal has gotten to your phone, you have no signal strength left,” he said. Osvaldik said that it was difficult to get signal through a Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA ) windshield. “You can have a million satellites up there with all the spectrum in the world, you can’t break the fundamental laws of physics," he said. Osvaldik also said that SpaceX would need “probably over a billion femtocells to have the equivalent outdoor coverage with all the interference problems.” A Femtocell is a device that improves indoor cellular coverage and data speeds. “It’s not a competitive threat” from a wireless perspective, Osvaldik said, but acknowledged that it could pose challenges in the broadband sector, as they can solve challenges with “spectral assets” and “external powered antennas,” Osvaldik said, adding that SpaceX could see success in the rural and suburban regions. Osvaldik also questioned SpaceX’s data center strategies. Speaking from the perspective of SpaceX’s management team, to criticize their strategy, he said “I have AI data centers with a payback of 1–1.5 years, and I’m gonna spend $100+ billion on building a non-competitive network. He added that either the company was “the world’s worst capital allocator” or that it was not going to happen. Earlier, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell had said during the company’s earnings call that it plans to take on traditional telecom companies with Starlink Mobile by end of 2027. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) also intends to unlock more than 1,000 MHz of additional spectrum for satellite broadband . SpaceX’s AI Compute Deal Notably, SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said that the company has signed a new agreement to offer compute capabilities that will result in a monthly revenue of more than $1 billion, while the annual recurring revenue (ARR) would go past $13 billion from the deal. SpaceX also has compute agreements in place with companies like Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) (NASDAQ: GOOG ) and Anthropic . The commercial spaceflight company also released the fourth-generation Starlink Router , promising better connectivity in congested areas, higher speeds and more.
